description: Cold-path helper for the git hook, which runs from a checkout and cannot reach the in-process door. Every other lock operation (acquire, try, wait, probe, guarantee, drain, clear-domain, predecessor state, holders) runs in the caller's process through the `holderLock` namespace of the combined addon. The helper judges whether a descriptor a process inherited is the very description that holds a lock (`--borrowed-check`), and answers one non-blocking shared try on a description the caller hands over (`--shared-try`).

exactlyOne.meaning: borrower test for hooks: fd 3 must have the same dev:ino as <path> and a non-blocking LOCK_EX on it must succeed (a description that already holds the lock succeeds; a sibling that opened the file itself fails). On Windows it takes no slot and uses FGOS_LOCK_JOB (holder-lock.port.v1.json borrowerCheck)

one non-blocking LOCK_SH attempt on fd 3; result free or held; the caller closes fd 3 afterwards. It never waits and never obstructs a holder. Windows answers unavailable (unsupported-platform): use --shared-try-path.

the same single non-blocking shared try on a fresh description the route opens itself, on every platform; it is how Windows probes. The existing file is opened read-only (never created, truncated or cleaned) and no predecessor admission runs. The lock is released and the handle closed before the answer is written. Answers free, held or unavailable like --shared-try; an unopenable file is an error.

fds.in: POSIX: fd 3 = the inherited description (O_RDWR). The helper sets FD_CLOEXEC on it before any other syscall. Windows: no slot is read.
fds.out: stdout = one JSON line then newline; stderr = free text for humans, never parsed

exitCodes.3: protocol mismatch (result error, code host-version-mismatch; --protocol absent or != 2)

invariants: the helper never takes a lock that outlives it and never calls LOCK_UN
the helper never leaves fd 3 open in a child it spawns (it spawns none)

callerRules.resolution: exec the binary named by FGOS_HOST_BIN or the activation, resolved once per process; never through a shim; never inside a hot lock
